newsitem.title: USA: CRP announcement "hopefully" this week - official.
newsitem.headline: CRP announcement "hopefully" this week - official.

text.p: The Agriculture Department will "hopefully" announce its new Conservation Reserve Program this week, a senior USDA official said Monday.

Parks Shackleford, asssistant deputy administrator for farm programs at the department, told reporters that the program is now being reviewed by the Office of Management and Budget, but that it will hopefully be cleared by week's end.

Shackleford spoke to reporters after a press conference by three groups representing various sectors of agribusiness who warned that the USDA appears to be about ready to open up the program to almost two-thirds of the nation's cropland, instead of targetting it to the most vulnerable and sensitive land.
"If in fact nearly two-thirds of the nation's land is eligible, that is environmental policy run amok," said Ken Cook of the Environmental Working Group.

Cook and other officials said there is already too much production land enrolled in the CRP, and that if USDA does not tighten its eligibility criteria, it would not resolve the problem of getting the really fragile land in the program.

In a letter to Cook responding to the concerns voiced by the groups Monday, Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said that the final rule will be focused on "highly erodible land and highly erodible cropland."
Glickman also said that reauthorization of the program at 36 million acres "helps to ensure that we have the means to retire lands from production where the environmental benefits can be maximized."

Glickman noted that there are some lands in the government's conservation compliance program that have not been eligible for the CRP that would provide even greater conservation benefits if the land were retired.

"If cropland is the conservation compliance program is in a key wildlife habitat area, or if it were to be devoted to top quality wildlife habitat when retired, its participation in the CRP may be of substantial environmental value."
